article.title: Common mistake: 'from' vs 'since' for time
article.description: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
article.content: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
